posts.text:
We're finally coming out of stealth at @WarpSciences! 🚀

A little story about how I ended up at Warp:

A few months ago, @shagunuppls and I were building a company around robotics infrastructure for scientific discovery. We had some amazing angels backing us and decided to reach out to @kevinweil, who previously led science initiatives at @OpenAI, hoping to get him on as an angel investor.

Turns out Kevin had been thinking about many of the same things, and somewhere in our conversations he floated a crazy idea: what if we joined forces?

I didn’t take it very seriously at first, but we cared so deeply about this mission that it was hard not to explore the idea. That led to a series of hours-long conversations with Kevin, @dpatil, and Sol. Somewhere along the way, we realized that we really enjoyed working together and had an unusually strong alignment on how we wanted to solve the technical problem and what kind of company we wanted to build.

Eventually, joining forces started to feel obvious. The mission stayed the same: accelerate the pace of science. But we now had the opportunity to make it much faster, bigger, and more ambitious.

We’ve spent the last few months heads down, building an incredible team and laying the foundations for what’s ahead.

And now, we're ready to show the world what we've been building.

posts.text:
A bit of late news.

A few months ago, I wrapped up an incredible chapter at @1x_tech.

I’m grateful to the team I worked with there, tackling one of the most ambitious  challenges in robotics.

Since then, @shagunuppls and I have been heads down building something new in robotics.

The last few months have been some of the most eventful and rewarding of my life. We've spent our days talking to scientists, roboticists, founders, researchers, and operators across a wide range of industries. Every conversation has reinforced our belief that robotics is at an inflection point, and that there are  many important problems worth solving.

We've also been fortunate to meet an incredible group of people who have believed in us early and helped shape what we're building.

Still very early, but we're excited for what's ahead.

Looking forward to sharing more soon.

posts.text:
World models matter because acting in the real world is expensive and unforgiving. If a robot can’t anticipate what will happen next, it has to learn everything the hard way. A world model gives it an internal sense of cause and effect — a way to think before it moves.

For NEO, that means learning in simulation instead of through endless real-world trial and error. At @1x_tech, we use world models to let NEO practice, test ideas, and understand how its actions change the environment before deploying them on hardware. It’s a faster, safer path to building robots that actually work in the real world.

He said science builds layer by layer, so he doesn’t think any single paper of his had that kind of immediate effect — and that very few researchers have.

One of the few he named was @ilyasut.
That’s why people should listen to this podcast.

Ilya breaks down the gap between strong eval performance and weaker real-world behavior, the pitfalls of current RL choices, and his view that humans don’t have general knowledge about every task — we have the ability to continually learn. 
A hint, perhaps, at what he’s focusing on now at @ssi.

posts.text:
Block laying off 4,000 people is tough to see. Layoffs are always painful, no matter how you frame them.

But it also feels like one of the first clear signals of AI-driven productivity actually showing up at scale inside big tech.

If you’ve been building with tools like @claudeai, @cursor_ai, etc., you’ve probably felt this shift already. The amount a small, focused team can ship today is kind of insane compared to even a year ago. Prototypes in days. Production features in weeks. Entire workflows automated.

That leverage compounds.

Credit to @jack for making sure severance was generous. That matters a lot in moments like this.

I don’t think this is a “doom” moment. It’s a transition moment. Some current software roles will shrink, yes. But new roles, new companies, and new layers of abstraction are being created just as fast.

We’re early in a big wave. 🌊

The real takeaway for anyone in tech: become indispensable. Learn the tools deeply. Don’t just use AI, rather build with it. Orchestrate it. Understand its limits.

The people who adapt fastest are going to have unfair leverage.

Exciting times ahead if you lean in 🚀🚀🚀
